title: GTA VI: The Album Spins Through Jazz, Hip-Hop, Pop, and More
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI took 13 years to make, and its music is just as big a deal as the game. The album works like a radio dial, jumping fast between very different styles — smooth jazz, hip-hop, pop, country, and blues. The first track, 'Starting From Zero,' pairs the electronic duo Justice, who wrote the game's music, with soul singer Michael McDonald. It feels like a classic buddy-cop movie theme. The closing track, 'Overtown Lights,' is a calm, late-night drive. Other tracks jump into today's sounds. 'That's It' teams rapper Yung Lean with rapper Future and producer Metro Boomin, mixing icy synths with trap beats and deep bass. The album also celebrates Spanish-language music, with Fuerza Regida's thumping 'Suzuki' and Helado Negro and Kali Uchis's dreamy breakup song 'Largate.' BLACKPINK's JENNIE rides robot-rocking synths on 'Power Trip.' With so many styles in one album, listening feels like spinning a radio dial and landing somewhere new every few minutes. That mix, the review says, makes it a snapshot of popular music right now.
why_it_matters: It shows how music can help tell a story in a game and introduce you to new kinds of songs.
